restored_invariants: Resource identity is derived from stable external object keys rather than mutable desired attributes.
Read paths use native Linux observers and remove missing or wrong-kind objects from Terraform refresh state without invoking Ansible.
Create and Update publish resulting state only after successful Ansible mutation and post-mutation observation.
Failed mutation paths return diagnostics without publishing the proposed successful transition.
Delete succeeds only for already-absent or successfully removed owned objects and verifies teardown where practical.
Named line, block and cron deletion remains scoped to the owned entry.
The process runner uses direct argv execution, caller context propagation, bounded timeout handling, non-zero exit failure and terminal temporary-file cleanup.
Map fingerprints and supplementary groups use deterministic ordering; modes and cron wildcard defaults use canonical forms.
Caller supplied source_digest participates in copy/template desired state and is validated against the local source file before mutation.
restart_idempotency_behavior: solve.sh overlays deterministic fixed source files, formats the provider tree and rebuilds the provider binary; it does not mutate verifier files, Terraform state or target resources directly.
determinism_notes: No random identifiers or wall-clock success criteria are introduced.
Stable IDs use path/name ownership keys.
Map and group ordering is canonicalized.
Execution errors are derived from actual process outcomes.
preserved_behavior: All ten resource schemas and local-Ansible execution model remain intact.
Terraform Core remains the only durable Terraform state owner.
The local Linux target remains the only supported target scope.
risks_for_independent_verifier: Verify Terraform Plugin Framework state-consistency behavior for required/configured attributes under refresh.
Verify ansible.builtin.cron absent-state invocation accepts the generated normalized argument set.
Verify copy destination drift produces the intended Terraform reconciliation plan through source_digest refresh semantics.
Exercise process cancellation and timeout against a controllable ansible-playbook shim.
Exercise user/group cases only with isolated test identities and guaranteed cleanup.
